chunks.title: Golden Verdict — The problem
chunks.text: Golden Verdict case study, The problem: Golden Verdict is a legal and tax compliance service for four kinds of user: Customers, Legal Partners, Managers and Administrators. Each of them needs a different view of the same applications, and access has to follow the role.

chunks.title: Golden Verdict — What I built
chunks.text:
Golden Verdict case study, What I built: I built it as a freelance project and it runs in production. Next.js, TypeScript, Firebase and Firestore, Tailwind CSS and the Brevo API make up the stack.
• The service workflow, end to end. A customer purchases a service, uploads documents and follows the application through a unique request ID, while status updates go out automatically. Firestore transactional operations and a scalable schema sit underneath.
• Admin dashboards for managing 50+ services, users, pricing and workflow assignments.
• Invoices and email generated and sent through the Brevo APIs.
• Security and reach: CSRF protection, secure session handling and SEO-optimised public service pages.

chunks.title: Golden Verdict — Key decisions
chunks.text:
Golden Verdict case study, Key decisions: Decision: Firestore transactions for request tracking. Why: A purchase touches more than one record: the request, its unique ID and its first status. A transaction makes those writes succeed or fail together. Trade-off: Transactions retry under contention and have size limits, so each one has to stay small and focused.

  Decision: Role-based access across four roles. Why: Every role sees the same applications differently. Keeping the permission rules in one place stops any dashboard from showing more than it should. Trade-off: Every new screen or action has to be mapped to a role up front, which is more design work than one shared dashboard.

  Decision: Brevo for invoices and email. Why: A dedicated API handles invoice generation and email delivery, so the app doesn't have to build either itself. Trade-off: The workflow now depends on a third-party service being available.

chunks.title: Golden Verdict — Architecture
chunks.text: Golden Verdict case study, Architecture: Follow a request from the customer to the admin dashboard. Hover or focus a component to see its job, or press Run request.

chunks.title: Golden Verdict — Outcome
chunks.text: Golden Verdict case study, Outcome: Golden Verdict is live in production. It serves four roles with role-based access, and its admin dashboards manage 50+ services.

chunks.title: Golden Verdict — Architecture components
chunks.text: Golden Verdict architecture, component by component: Customer — One of four roles. Buys a service, uploads documents and tracks the application with a unique request ID. Next.js app — The web app: SEO-optimised public service pages plus a dashboard for each role. Auth · RBAC — Role-based access control for Customers, Legal Partners, Managers and Administrators, with CSRF protection and secure session handling. Firestore — Service purchases and status updates are written with Firestore transactional operations on a scalable schema. Every application gets a unique request ID. Brevo — Brevo APIs generate invoices automatically and send email. Admin dashboard — Administrators manage 50+ services, users, pricing and workflow assignments.

chunks.title: Talnio — The problem
chunks.text: Talnio case study, The problem: Talnio is an employee management platform. It has to work on web and on mobile, with the same data in step on both, and cover attendance, analytics, meetings and day-to-day productivity.

chunks.title: Talnio — What I built
chunks.text:
Talnio case study, What I built: I built and shipped Talnio as App Developer Intern at Social Agent (Bricstal Pvt. Ltd.), Bengaluru, from May 2025. The web app uses React 19 and Tailwind CSS, the mobile app uses Flutter and Dart, and both sit on Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore real-time sync.
• Attendance based on geolocation and NFC, with automated PDF and Excel reports that power workforce analytics.
• Live video and audio meetings through the Agora SDK.
• AI automation: Google Generative AI APIs automate productivity workflows.

chunks.title: Talnio — Key decisions
chunks.text:
Talnio case study, Key decisions: Decision: Firestore real-time sync as the shared backbone. Why: Both clients subscribe to the same data, so a change on one shows up on the other without polling or a manual refresh. Trade-off: Live listeners keep reading as data changes, so queries need to be scoped tightly to stay efficient.

  Decision: A Flutter app and a React web app. Why: Mobile and web have different strengths: device features such as location and NFC on one, wide dashboards and reports on the other. Trade-off: Two codebases to keep consistent, so shared behaviour has to live in the data model rather than in shared UI code.

  Decision: SDKs and APIs for meetings and AI. Why: Video and audio calls and language models are specialised problems. Agora and Google Generative AI let the product add them as integrations. Trade-off: Each adds an external dependency and its own failure modes.

chunks.title: Talnio — Architecture
chunks.text: Talnio case study, Architecture: Pick a flow, then press Run request to send it through the system. The meetings and AI paths branch off the client apps.

chunks.title: Talnio — Outcome
chunks.text: Talnio case study, Outcome: Talnio is live on Google Play. It delivers attendance, analytics reports, meetings and AI automation on web and mobile, with real-time sync between them.

chunks.title: Talnio — Architecture components
chunks.text: Talnio architecture, component by component: Mobile / Web — The Flutter mobile app and the React 19 web app. Attendance uses geolocation and NFC. Firebase Auth — Firebase Authentication signs users in on both platforms. Cloud Firestore — Real-time sync keeps web and mobile in step. Report generator — Automated PDF/Excel reports power workforce analytics. Agora SDK — Powers live video and audio meetings. Google Gen AI — Google Generative AI APIs automate productivity workflows.

chunks.title: LanSymphony — The problem
chunks.text: LanSymphony case study, The problem: Communication that works on a local network with no server and no internet connection, and stays private while doing it.

chunks.title: LanSymphony — What I built
chunks.text:
LanSymphony case study, What I built: LanSymphony is a serverless, internet-free communication system for local networks, written in Python with sockets and multi-threading. I built it live at the Windsurf × The AI Collective OpenBuild in Bengaluru.
• Security and discovery: AES-256 encryption and automatic peer discovery, on a multi-threaded architecture.
• Calls: HD video calling, VoIP audio and screen sharing, with customisable quality and Picture-in-Picture.

chunks.title: LanSymphony — Key decisions
chunks.text:
LanSymphony case study, Key decisions: Decision: Peer-to-peer with automatic discovery. Why: With no central server there is nothing to host and nothing that needs the internet. Peers find each other on the network by themselves. Trade-off: Every client carries the networking logic, and peers have to discover each other without help.

  Decision: AES-256 for everything on the wire. Why: Other devices on a shared local network can see its traffic. Encryption keeps the conversation private. Trade-off: Encrypting every frame costs CPU, which matters most for real-time video.

  Decision: A multi-threaded architecture. Why: Video, audio and screen sharing run at the same time and shouldn't block one another. Trade-off: Threads bring synchronisation and shutdown complexity that a single loop avoids.

chunks.title: LanSymphony — Architecture
chunks.text: LanSymphony case study, Architecture: From discovery to a live call. Hover or focus a step for details, or press Run request to walk through a connection.

chunks.title: LanSymphony — Outcome
chunks.text: LanSymphony case study, Outcome: LanSymphony placed 2nd at the Windsurf × The AI Collective OpenBuild in Bengaluru, among 20+ teams, in August 2025.

chunks.title: LanSymphony — Architecture components
chunks.text: LanSymphony architecture, component by component: Peer discovery — Peers find each other automatically on the local network — no server, no internet. Key exchange — Peers agree on a session key before any media flows. AES-256 channel — Traffic is encrypted with AES-256. A multi-threaded architecture keeps connections running side by side. Video · VoIP · Screen — HD video calling, VoIP audio and screen sharing with customisable quality and Picture-in-Picture.

chunks.title: CHRIST University Virtual Tour — The problem
chunks.text: CHRIST University Virtual Tour case study, The problem: A way to explore the CHRIST University campus in 360 degrees, from a browser on a laptop or a phone.

chunks.title: CHRIST University Virtual Tour — What I built
chunks.text:
CHRIST University Virtual Tour case study, What I built: An immersive 360° web experience in React, Three.js and TypeScript, deployed on Vercel.
• Interactive hotspots on the panorama, with multimedia integration.
• Smooth navigation controls for moving around the campus.
• Responsive design, optimised for web and mobile.

chunks.title: CHRIST University Virtual Tour — Key decisions
chunks.text:
CHRIST University Virtual Tour case study, Key decisions: Decision: Three.js for the panorama. Why: A 360° scene is a 3D problem. Three.js renders it in the browser without a plugin. Trade-off: WebGL scenes are heavier than static pages, so performance on phones needs care.

  Decision: Hotspots as an interactive layer. Why: Hotspots turn a passive panorama into a guided tour and keep multimedia one click away. Trade-off: Each hotspot is content that someone has to place and maintain.

  Decision: Responsive from the start. Why: A tour is only useful if it works wherever it's opened, on a desktop browser or a phone. Trade-off: Mouse and touch controls both have to feel right, which adds interaction testing.

chunks.title: CHRIST University Virtual Tour — Architecture
chunks.text: CHRIST University Virtual Tour case study, Architecture: From the React app to the media behind each hotspot. Hover or focus a layer for its job, or press Run request.

chunks.title: CHRIST University Virtual Tour — Outcome

chunks.text: CHRIST University Virtual Tour architecture, component by component: React app — Responsive web app, optimised for web and mobile and deployed on Vercel.
